```{r meta, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE}
library(data.table)
library(stringr)

# Fetch live metadata from your package
meta_file <- system.file("extdata", "metadata.csv", package = "ariadneDB")

meta <- fread(meta_file)

meta$resource <-  str_split_i(meta$Title, "\\s+", 2L)

meta <- meta[ , c("resource", "FullName", "WebUrl", "License")]

meta <- meta[!duplicated(meta), ]
```

# Introduction

The way that ariadne retrieves and combines relational data is informed by its
companion data package [ariadneDB](https://github.com/Minotau-R/ariadneDB),
which contains information about the feature types and mappings available from
a handful of popular databases. From here on, we will refer to those databases
as _resources_ to distinguish them from the ariadne database itself.

The relational information of each resource is described by a graph, where nodes
and edges represent feature types and mappings between them, respectively. In
ariadneDB, these graphs are stored in the Graph Modelling Language (GML), which
is a standard format for relational data. Currently, ariadneDB includes
`r nrow(meta)` resources that span a diverse set of biological domains and
applications.

```{r restbl, echo = FALSE, message = FALSE}
library(dplyr)

# Define only the vignette-specific metadata & citation keys
annotations <- list(
    BugSigDB = c(
        desc = "Literature-based association of signature taxa by phenotype",
        reference = "@geistlinger2024bugsigdb"
    ),
    ChocoPhlAn = c(
        desc = "Pangenome database resulting from the ChocoPhlAn pipeline",
        reference = "@franzosa2018species"
    ),
    enviPath = c(
        desc = "Environmental contaminant biotransformation pathway database",
        reference = "@hafner2024envipath"
    ),
    GM = c(
        desc = "Legacy versions of gut metabolic modules and gut brain modules",
        reference = "@vieira2016species; @valles2019neuroactive"
    ),
    GO = c(
        desc = "Controlled vocabulary of gene and gene product attributes",
        reference = "@ashburner2000gene"
    ),
    KEGG = c(
        desc = "Metabolic pathway database linking ko and ec to reactions, pathways and organisms",
        reference = "@kanehisa2000kegg"
    ),
    MSigDB = c(
        desc = "Molecular Signatures Database of annotated gene sets",
        reference = "@subramanian2005gene"
    ),
    OTT = c(
        desc = "Synthetic tree of life constructed by combining public phylogenetic trees and taxonomic data",
        reference = "@hinchliff2015synthesis"
    ),
    Rhea = c(
        desc = "The reactome database",
        reference = "@bansal2022rhea"
    ),
    TIGRFAMs = c(
        desc = "Protein family definitions for functional annotation",
        reference = "@haft2001tigrfams"
    ),
    UniProt = c(
        desc = "The proteome database",
        reference = "@bateman2025uniprot"
    ),
    WoL = c(
        desc = "Biological network database",
        reference = "@zhu2019phylogenomics"
    )
)

ann_df <- bind_rows(annotations, .id = "resource")

# Merge, build markdown strings and select final columns
tbl <- meta |>
    left_join(ann_df, by = "resource") |>
    mutate(
        Title = ifelse(
            is.na(FullName), resource, sprintf("%s (%s)", FullName, resource)
        ),
        Resource = sprintf(
            '<a href="%s" target="_blank" rel="noopener">%s</a>',
            WebUrl, Title
        ),
        License = coalesce(License, "—")
    ) |>
    select(
        Resource,
        Description = desc,
        License,
        Reference = reference
    )
```

```{r echo = FALSE, results = 'asis'}
# Build a mapping table so each row has a unique placeholder ID
cite_df <- tbl |>
    mutate(
        .row_idx = row_number(),
        .span_id = sprintf("cite-src-%d", .row_idx),
        .cite_md = Reference,
        Citation = sprintf(
            '<span class="cite-slot" data-target-row="%d"></span>',
            .row_idx - 1L
        )
    ) |>
    select(Resource, Citation, .cite_md, .span_id)

# Emit raw @citations so Pandoc's citeproc renders them in-place
cat('<div id="pandoc-cite-staging" style="display:none;">\n')

for (i in seq_len(nrow(cite_df))) {
    cat(sprintf(
        '<span id="%s">%s</span>\n', cite_df$.span_id[i], cite_df$.cite_md[i]
    ))
}

cat('\n</div>\n')
```

```{r echo = FALSE, message = FALSE}
library(DT)
library(htmlwidgets)
library(jsonlite)

datatable(
    tbl,
    escape = FALSE,
    options = list(drawCallback = JS(sprintf("
        function(settings) {
            var api = this.api();
            var map = %s;
            api.rows({page: 'current'}).nodes().each(function(rowNode, idx) {
                var rowIdx = api.row(rowNode).index();
                var srcId = map[rowIdx];
                var renderedHtml = $('#' + srcId).html();
                if (renderedHtml) {
                    $('td', rowNode).eq(4).html(renderedHtml);
                }
           });
        }
    ", toJSON(cite_df$.span_id, auto_unbox = TRUE))))
)
```

# Tutorial

This tutorial demonstrates how to import and explore the ariadne resource graph.
First, we set up the environment by loading the necessary dependencies.

```{r lib, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
# Load required packages
library(ariadne)
library(igraph)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(DT)
```

When `ariadne()` is executed, the graph for each resource is retrieved from the
database release on [Zenodo](https://zenodo.org/records/18788725) and combined
into a single igraph object.

```{r fetch}
# Import resource graph
graph <- ariadne()

# Plot resource graph
plotPath(graph)
```

Some resources have multiple versions, which can be selected through the
argument `versions`. This defaults to the latest version found in the database.

```{r res_versions}
# List available resource versions
versions <- listResourceVersions()

# View versions
datatable(versions)
```

The igraph object is made of two components: edges data and nodes (or vertices)
data, which are stored in two different data tables.

```{r graph2df}
# Convert igraph to data.frame pair
graph_df <- igraph::as_data_frame(graph, what = "both")

# Extract edges data
edge_df <- graph_df$edges
# Extract nodes data
node_df <- graph_df$vertices
```

As mentioned above, the resource graph is composed of feature types (nodes) and
mappings (edges) from several resources. We generate the summary statistics for
each resource integrated within ariadne.

```{r stats}
# Get stats for each resource
df <- edge_df |>
    group_by(source) |>
    summarise(edges = n(), nodes = n_distinct(c(from, to)))

# View stats
datatable(df)
```

The number of edges and nodes represent the amount of links and feature types
provided by each resource, respectively. These two metrics largely vary between
the available resources. The size and graph for each resource can be visualized
by generating individual graphs with the argument `res.name`.

```{r plot_graphs}
# Create resource graphs
plots <- lapply(
    df$source, function(x) {
        plotPath(graph, res.name = x, layout = "stress", focus = TRUE) +
            ggtitle(x)
    }
)

# View resource graphs
plots
```

As seen in the graphs, each resource includes unique links between different
feature types, which ariadneDB integrates into a single organised graph to
benefit from its emerging properties.
